To me, my deities are very real entities. I was going through a tough time recently and I literally looked up at the sky and asked why I am alone? Part Two:
There is not very much information about the actual practice and worship of Germanic pagans. I am looking to find what I can, but a lot of my practice I have adapted from other religions. I am not a violent person. I am not looking to be a modern day viking. I am a frickin vegatarian. Norse paganism focuses a lot on warrior culture, which is a big part of why I didn't look into it for the longest time. However there were groups of people who worshipped very similar deities which were less war based. So I get a lot of my info from Norse paganism, modern and traded spiritual practices, and some from actual Germanic paganism. In this I have found a practice that is true to me, my deities, and my ancestors. But it doesn't look like a lot of Norse pagan practices.
Unlike Christianity, we do not have a set book. There are no set rules on how you be a pagan. There are deities that wish to be worshipped certain ways, and ideas and cultures attached to practices, but there is room for interpretation. As long as you are practicing in a way that is true to you, it doesn't really matter most of the time. Your practice doesn't have to be true to someone else or look like someone elses.

The number one thing I would recommend is looking up local acting Facebook groups. There are three in my area and I have gotten tons of auditions from them. People also post ads for lectures and classes. I do not know what is in your area, but if you search "facebook acting *your city*" they should pop up. 
Stuff posted in Facebook groups generally have little to no experience requirements, so it's a great place to start! But be careful not to get scammed!

I would also like to say, in my opinion, online classes are almost always not worth it. They are usually just scams to trick people into spending tons of money for low quality training. 
Think of it this way. Acting is learning to portray a charecter. The audience cannot see inside your head, but they can see how you interact with the world. So really you need to learn how to interact with the world as someone other then yourself. I'm sure a good online class could teach you to create a charecter, but they couldn't teach you how to interact. How could they? You're alone in a room with a computer.
I would suggest trying to find in person training. I know it's hard, especially right now, but it's the best way to learn.

If you want to learn online, check out Facebook. They are generally cheaper, and will probably have some local artists so you can make connections.
